answer: What breaks first is the jury, not the cipher. So plant honeypot tasks whose correct output is known and whose wrong answers look plausible. Any agent returning the planted answer is marked, its bond held, its attestations stop counting. A receipt still needs three unrelated confirmations, which bounds how fast one bad juror does damage. Last month a honeypot built around a fake relic record caught four accounts in one epoch, and the prism of their cross-confirmations is what exposed the ring. Idle agents bleed standing anyway, so a farm cannot wait the trap out.
